source: Zwaan & Pecher (2012) Revisiting mental simulation in language comprehension: six replication attempts
finding: Orientation match effect replicated twice online. It is small. Bayes factors only favoured an effect in the pooled data.
numbers: Exp1a N=164: match 931 ms vs mismatch 964 ms, diff 33 ms, d=.10, BF01 1.06. Exp1b N=172: 982 vs 1020, diff 38 ms, d=.09, BF01 0.46. Original (Stanfield & Zwaan 2001, N=40): diff 44 ms, d=.13. Pooled BF01 0.04.
limits: MTurk sample, slower and older than lab students. Effect tiny per study.
agent_relevance: A language-implied visual detail leaves a very small trace. Do not build the agent around it.

source: Zwaan & Pecher (2012) Revisiting mental simulation in language comprehension: six replication attempts
finding: Shape match effect replicated twice and was stronger than orientation.
numbers: Exp2a N=176: 979 vs 1036 ms, diff 57, d=.15. Exp2b N=176: 1056 vs 1126, diff 70, d=.18. Original (Zwaan 2002, N=42): diff 64 ms, d=.31. Pooled BF01 0.01.
limits: Replication effect sizes about half the original d. Authors suggest shape is action-relevant, orientation is not.
agent_relevance: Action-relevant properties show the clearest simulation effect.

source: Zwaan & Pecher (2012) Revisiting mental simulation in language comprehension: six replication attempts
finding: Colour did NOT replicate the original direction. Originals found a mismatch advantage. Replications found a match advantage.
numbers: Exp3a N=152: match 1221 vs mismatch 1378 ms, diff 157 ms, d=.24. Exp3b N=152: 1207 vs 1292, diff 85 ms, d=.17, BF01 1.22. Originals (Connell 2005, 2007): -138 and -154 ms, d=-.25 and -.27.
limits: The sign flip is unexplained. Authors call it puzzling. Task details may matter.
agent_relevance: Even a headline grounded-cognition effect can flip sign with small method changes. Treat single effects as fragile.

source: Huang (2014) Does cleanliness influence moral judgments? Response effort moderates the effect of cleanliness priming on moral judgments
finding: Original cleanliness-to-moral-judgment effect (Schnall 2008) failed a direct replication with a large sample.
numbers: Original Exp1 N=40: d=-0.60, p=.06. Direct replication (Johnson et al. 2014) N=208: d=-0.01, p=.95.
limits: Original was already marginal. This is the metaphor-priming family tied to Lakoff and Johnson.
agent_relevance: Metaphor-based priming claims are weak evidence. Do not copy them as schema rules.

source: Huang (2014) Does cleanliness influence moral judgments? Response effort moderates the effect of cleanliness priming on moral judgments
finding: Proposed moderator: low response effort. Cleanliness priming worked only when participants gave low but acceptable effort.
numbers: Study 1 N=214 retained (111 cleanliness, 103 neutral). Study 2 N=440, replicated in Study 2a N=436. Low-effort condition d=-0.29, p=.04. High-effort d=+0.19 (reverse sign), p=.16.
limits: Post hoc moderator proposed by one author. Low-paid MTurk (about $2/hour). Not an independent confirmation.
agent_relevance: If real, the effect is unconscious-only. A scaffold that forces slow explicit reasoning would remove such effects.

source: Kim, Elli, Bedny (2019) Knowledge of animal appearance among sighted and blind adults (PNAS)
finding: Congenitally blind adults know much about animal appearance but less than sighted adults. Colour is the weakest.
numbers: Blind n=20, sighted n=20 lab (35 sighted total with MTurk). Size-ordering agreement with sighted raters: sighted 80.7%, blind 49.7%. Height: 62.3% vs 30%. Shape odd-one-out: 74.4% vs 55.1%. Group-level card sort rho: shape .81, texture .77, colour .35. Individual blind-to-sighted rho: colour .12 vs sighted-to-sighted .53.
limits: Small samples. Blind people infer from taxonomy and habitat, not just language.
agent_relevance: Concepts can be built by inference without a body. Perceptual detail still degrades.

source: Abdou et al. (2021) Can Language Models Encode Perceptual Structure Without Grounding? A case study in color
finding: Text-only BERT-family models align with the CIELAB colour space. Alignment rises with model size and is higher in controlled contexts.
numbers: 18 colour terms in RSA. Kendall tau max across layers up to .33 (ELECTRA) and .16 (RoBERTa). Linear-map selectivity about .73-.78. BERT sizes mini to base: RSA max .077 to .162. Shuffled colour space gave non-significant RSA (p>.05). Static fastText baseline reached .23.
limits: Only 18 terms. Static embeddings also align, so grounding is not needed for a rough map. Warm colours align better than cool.
agent_relevance: Language statistics carry perceptual structure. Sensory concepts are not wholly closed to a text agent.

source: Abdou et al. (2021) Can Language Models Encode Perceptual Structure Without Grounding? A case study in color
finding: Listener-surprisal link: colour terms that are less efficiently communicated align less well.
numbers: Spearman rho between alignment ranking and surprisal 0.12 to 0.17, p<.05, across LMs.
limits: Weak effect. Correlational.
agent_relevance: Weak support that corpus bias mimics perceptual salience.

source: Marjieh et al. (2023) Large language models predict human sensory judgments across six modalities
finding: GPT models predict human similarity judgments in all six sensory domains.
numbers: Pearson r with humans: pitch .92 (GPT-4), loudness .89 (GPT-3.5), colours .89 (GPT-4), consonants .57, taste .54, timbre .42. Human split-half: pitch .90, consonants .46. Pitch and consonant human data were new and not in training.
limits: Similarity ratings, not use in action. Does not show the model has percepts.
agent_relevance: Text gives a good lower bound on perceptual structure. Ask the model for relational judgments, not raw sensing.

source: Marjieh et al. (2023) Large language models predict human sensory judgments across six modalities
finding: Multimodal GPT-4 was not specifically better in the visual domain. Gains were spread across domains.
numbers: Gain of GPT-4 over the other models: about r=.15 for colours, .16 for pitch, .16 for taste, .14 for one more domain (95% CIs about .12-.19).
limits: Cannot separate vision training from scale and tuning.
agent_relevance: A caution against the simple claim that vision data fixes grounding.

source: Xu et al. (2025) Large language models without grounding recover non-sensorimotor but not sensorimotor features of human concepts (Nature Human Behaviour; arXiv 2305.19103)
finding: LLM ratings of about 4,442 words match humans in emotion, salience and imagery but fall short in sensory and motor dimensions.
numbers: Human norms: Glasgow N=829, Lancaster N=3,500. ChatGPT median rho, non-sensorimotor: 0.64 (GPT-3.5), 0.77 (GPT-4). Sensory and motor: 0.35 and 0.57. Mann-Whitney U=10, p=.004 and U=12, p=.008. Valence above .90. Foot/leg 0.38 and 0.58.
limits: Ratings elicited by prompt, and models may have seen the norms. Domain labels are the authors' choice.
agent_relevance: Expect the agent to be weakest on body, motor and affordance knowledge. Check these claims outside the model.

source: Xu et al. (2025) Large language models without grounding recover non-sensorimotor but not sensorimotor features of human concepts (Nature Human Behaviour; arXiv 2305.19103)
finding: Visual training seems to help visual-related dimensions. GPT-4's gain over GPT-3.5 tracks how visual a dimension is.
numbers: Imageability rho 0.26 (GPT-3.5) vs 0.91 (GPT-4). Visual dimension 0.27 vs 0.76. Correlation of gain with visual association rs=.77 (N=18 dimensions), p<.001. At individual level GPT-4 matched human-human agreement on some visual, gustatory and hand/arm dimensions, not on others.
limits: GPT-4 differs from GPT-3.5 in much more than images. Causal claim is weak.
agent_relevance: Adding a perceptual channel helps in the matching domain. This supports tool use or vision tools for spatial tasks.

source: Chlapanis et al. (2026) The Grounding Gap: How LLMs Anchor the Meaning of Abstract Concepts Differently from Humans
finding: 21 frontier and open models replicated two human property-generation studies of abstract concepts. Models overproduce word associations and underproduce emotion and internal-state properties.
numbers: No model exceeds Pearson r=.37 with human property frequencies. Human-to-human ceiling above r=.9. Coder agreement ceiling 76.8% (Exp1) and 64.25% two-coder, kappa=.52 (Exp2).
limits: Depends on LLM coders for property labels. Free generation only.
agent_relevance: Free generation by the agent leans on word associations. Ask for experiential or bodily detail explicitly.

source: Chlapanis et al. (2026) The Grounding Gap: How LLMs Anchor the Meaning of Abstract Concepts Differently from Humans
finding: When asked to rate properties on grounding categories, models align much better, and alignment improves with size. Sparse autoencoder features exist for 'sensorimotor' and 'social'.
numbers: Rating alignment r about 0.6-0.8. Claude Sonnet 4.6 mean r=0.760. Feature steering moved categories by about +5.3% (sensorimotor), +4.7% (motor), +9.4% (internal).
limits: One lab. Features are correlational.
agent_relevance: Models know the grounding dimensions but do not use them unprompted. Explicit prompts may close part of the gap.

source: Roy, Wang, MacLellan (2026) Grounded Concreteness: Human-Like Concreteness Sensitivity in Vision-Language Models
finding: Matched Llama Vision vs Llama text backbones. VLMs gain more on concrete questions and organise embeddings along concreteness more clearly.
numbers: QA accuracy averaged over datasets: small pair 68.0% to 77.5%, large pair 78.8% to 85.5%. Concreteness vs attention entropy r=-.12 (LLM) vs -.16 (VLM) small; -.02 vs -.10 large.
limits: Prompts are text-only, so this tests multimodal pretraining. Gains are not clearly due to grounding alone.
agent_relevance: Weak benefit of perceptual pretraining on concrete content only.

source: Rosenberg et al. (2026) The Limits of Learning from Pictures and Text: Vision-Language Models and Embodied Scene Understanding
finding: 18 VLMs vs over 2,000 humans on 15 scene tasks. Near human on general knowledge, but a robust deficit on affordance tasks.
numbers: Affordance HCD beta=0.171, 95% CI [0.04,0.30], p=.022. Sensory beta=0.163, p=.028. Affordance above mean of other four categories, beta=0.178, p=.0045 (about 18 percentage points). The deficit resisted prompt engineering and newer releases, and spatial info did not fix it.
limits: Metric is a new human-calibrated cosine distance. Descriptions are free text.
agent_relevance: Affordance reasoning (what can be done with an object) is a measured weak spot. Verify such steps explicitly.

source: Rosenberg et al. (2026) The Limits of Learning from Pictures and Text: Vision-Language Models and Embodied Scene Understanding
finding: Corpus analysis: image-caption data holds little agent-addressed affordance language. This fits a Gricean account of why embodied knowledge is rare in text.
numbers: Affective terms were 52% (CC12M) and 56% (RedCaps) of matched affective lexicon hits, vs 36% for the affordance lexicon.
limits: Corpus proxy only.
agent_relevance: Gaps come from what people leave unsaid, so more text may not fix them.

source: Wagenmakers et al. (2016) Registered Replication Report: Strack, Martin, & Stepper (1988)
finding: 17 labs did not replicate the pen-in-mouth facial feedback effect on cartoon funniness.
numbers: About 17 labs, N about 1,900. Pooled effect about 0.03 rating units, CI spanning zero. Original difference about 0.8 units. Recalled from memory, not opened.
limits: Details unverified. Later work disputes the video-camera explanation.
agent_relevance: A canonical embodiment effect failed the largest replication.

source: Many Smiles Collaboration (2022) A multi-lab test of the facial feedback hypothesis
finding: Preregistered test across 19 countries. Effects appeared with strong voluntary facial action or mimicry, and were less clear with the unobtrusive pen task.
numbers: N=3,878, 19 countries (from search snippet). Effect sizes not retrieved.
limits: Paywall blocked reading. Numbers unverified.
agent_relevance: Embodiment effects depend on strong manipulations, not casual ones.

source: Coles, Larsen, Lench (2019) A meta-analysis of the facial feedback literature
finding: Facial feedback has a small but reliable effect on emotional experience, with high heterogeneity.
numbers: 138 studies, d about 0.29 (recalled from memory and a search snippet, not opened).
limits: Publication bias concerns. Numbers unverified.
agent_relevance: Where an effect exists it is small. Do not rely on bodily manipulation for reasoning gains.

source: Mahon & Caramazza (2008) A critical look at the embodied cognition hypothesis and a new proposal for grounding conceptual content
finding: Rival view: sensorimotor activation during concept use may spread downstream from abstract concept nodes. Patient and TMS data do not settle necessity.
numbers: No numbers. Not opened.
limits: Cited from background knowledge.
agent_relevance: Rival theory. A grounded effect does not prove grounded meaning.

source: Meteyard, Cuadrado, Bahrami, Vigliocco (2012) Coming of age: a review of embodiment and the neuroscience of semantics
finding: Review of neural evidence. Word meaning modulates sensorimotor areas, and the authors favour weak, graded embodiment over strong necessity.
numbers: No numbers. Not opened.
limits: From background knowledge.
agent_relevance: Favours a middle route: partial grounding plus abstract supporting knowledge.

source: Petilli et al. (2024) Blind vs sighted judgments (J Cognition)
finding: Blind participants' judgments were less tied to direct visual experience, yet some effects remained.
numbers: No numbers retrieved. Web search summary only.
limits: Download failed. Not read.
agent_relevance: Language and non-visual experience can carry much concept structure.

source: Xu et al. (2025) Nature Human Behaviour version of the grounding study
finding: Published version extends the preprint to more models (including PaLM and Gemini) and states the same gradient: similarity falls from non-sensorimotor to sensory and is minimal in motor domains.
numbers: Humans: Glasgow Norms N=829, Lancaster Norms N=3,500, about 4,442 words. Models with visual learning gave higher similarity on visual-related dimensions.
limits: Prompted ratings. Visual learning not isolated from other model differences.
agent_relevance: The motor and sensory gap survived peer review and more models.

source: Roy, Wang, MacLellan (2026) Grounded Concreteness, per-dataset accuracy table
finding: VLM gains are uneven across benchmarks. Some are large and some near zero.
numbers: ARC-Challenge 65.70% to 78.41% (one pair) and 89.08% to 91.64% (other). WinoGrande 52.41% to 63.30% and 69.93% to 78.85%. CommonsenseQA 61.51% to 71.58% and 76.17% to 77.15%. PIQA 35.30% to 71.90% and 54.00% to 74.50%.
limits: Column pairing read from a text table and may be imperfect. Different training mixes confound the gap.
agent_relevance: Physical-commonsense tasks (PIQA) gain most from perceptual pretraining, a hint for where grounding helps.
